Request for Proposals
Project Name:

Utilities Technology Master Plan (UTMP)
and Customer Information System (CIS)
Consulting Services
Project ID’s: 00.25.513 and 00.25.521

2026003

Proposal Due Time:

2:00 P.M.
All responses must be submitted electronically through the Bonfire platform.
Hard copy submittals are not accepted.

this solicitation.

and to waive any and all informalities.

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

Scope of Services
Utility Services Overview
Indian River County (IRC) is located in the southeastern and east-central portions of Florida.

Seated in Vero Beach,
the County has approximately 503 square miles of land area.
As of the 2023 census, the population was 169,795.

The IRC Department of Utility Services (IRCDUS) was formed over 30 years ago when the County’s water,
wastewater, and solid waste utility services were consolidated under one department within Indian River County
Board of County Commissioners (BCC).

Today, IRCDUS provides water, wastewater, and solid waste services to
a population of over 150,000.

The water system, the largest in the County, provides service to over 57,000 accounts, including residential and
commercial customers within an urban service area (USA) of approximately 41 square miles.

The water system
includes two (2) water production facilities (WPF) with a total of sixteen (16) source water wells, two (2)
demineralized concentrate treatment facilities, approximately nine hundred (900) miles of transmission and
distribution pipelines, and ten (10) million gallons of treated water storage.

The wastewater system, with four (4)
water reclamation facilities (WRF), over four-hundred and eighty-four (484) miles of sanitary sewers, and fourhundred and twenty-eight (428) lift stations, is also the largest such system in the County and serves approximately
38,000 accounts.

IRCDUS maintains and operates a reuse system comprising approximately forty-five (45) miles
of pipeline, three-million gallons of storage, and supply pumping facilities.

The Solid Waste Disposal District (SWDD) is a dependent district of IRC created by the BCC on June 20, 1995,
pursuant to the authority and procedures of Chapter 125.01(5)(a), Laws of Florida.

SWDD provides for the disposal
of all Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) generated in IRC at the IRC landfill as well as five (5) Customer Convenience
Centers (CCC’s).

Its purpose is to have an efficient and environmentally sound solid and hazardous waste
management system to prevent disease spreading, to promote orderly growth within the County, and to meet
existing and projected demands for waste management, including collection and disposal of solid waste, yard waste,
bulk waste and recyclables.

SWDD has begun utilizing a leachate evaporator for leachate management via a
partnership with Indian River Sustainability Center which concentrates the leachate for disposal back into the
landfill and emits water vapor.

SWDD also captures landfill gas to create Renewable Natural Gas under a private
partnership.
SWDD funding is from non-ad valorem assessments and tipping fees.

RFP Intent
This Project represents a dual-purpose engagement.

The selected Consultant will:
1.

UTMP Development: Develop a strategic, forward-looking UTMP to guide IRCDUS modernization
efforts and technology investments over the next five (5) years.

CIS Selection: Lead a structured process of assessments, requirements gathering, and evaluation of vendor
solutions, that will lead to the selection of a best-fit CIS solution that aligns with IRCDUS operational goals
and the County’s enterprise IT architecture.

This RFP is intended to provide potential Firms or Consultants with the necessary information to build a Proposal
that meets IRCDUS’s needs.

Proposals should address the objectives, tasks, and deliverables detailed in this RFP
and provide information on the Firm’s practices, experience, and offerings that will meet or exceed the IRCDUS’s
expectations.

The Scope of Services for the UTMP includes a comprehensive review of IRCDUS’s existing business processes,
information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) environments, staffing levels and competencies, to

Page 2 of 16

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

identify gaps and opportunities relative to best practices and future-state vision, and the development of a strategic
digital roadmap and associated budgets aligned with the BCC Strategic Goals.

In July 2010, IRCDUS selected CIS Infinity, a widely used Customer Information and Billing System developed
by Advanced Utility Systems/Harris Computer, to replace its aging utility billing application.

The implementation
saw full “go-live” status by November 2011, with CIS Infinity formally in production.

The transition included
integration with external credit/debit tools (e.g., ONLINE Utility Exchange) to enhance delinquency management
and credit risk mitigation.

The CIS Infinity deployment represented a significant technological investment, yielding
several operational improvements.
Over a decade since its deployment, CIS Infinity continues to support essential utility functions.

However, growth
in utility demand, complexity in rate management, increasing customer expectations, evolving regulatory
requirements, expanded customer service needs, the shift toward cloud infrastructure, and the County’s broader IT
modernization goals have rendered the system due for a reassessment.

More specifically:



The existing maintenance contract is nearing expiration, necessitating timely strategic planning and
decision-making.

IRCDUS and the County now aim to optimize its wider technology transformation by evaluating the
feasibility of on-premises architecture versus cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform for its
future-state.

As a mission-critical system with a direct impact on customer service and revenue management, the CIS is one of
IRCDUS most significant technology assets.
Replacing it with a modern SaaS solution is a strategic priority.

As
such, the selected Firm will also assist IRCDUS in assessing its CIS requirements, evaluating upgrade and/or
replacement options, and supporting the selection of the new CIS solution that meets the Department’s customer
service, business, operational, and technical objectives.

Firms are required to be independent and have no business,
personal nor financial affiliations with any CIS vendor.

IRCDUS also requires Firms to provide objective and
vendor-neutral perspectives, as well as exercise discretion and confidentiality during the CIS evaluation and
selection process.

Current Technology Landscape
This information is confidential per F.S.

119.0725, is incorporated into this request for proposals, and will be
provided after execution of a non-disclosure agreement (NDA).
Every proposer must review this document;

and
proposals submitted by firms that have not accessed the document will be rejected.

The NDA is provided in the
public files section of Bonfire, and shall be submitted, with evidence of authority to sign, via email to
purchasing@indianriver.gov no less than 14 days prior to the due date for proposals.

IRCDUS Key Priorities
IRCDUS is committed to modernizing its operations and strengthening long-term organizational resilience.

As the
County experiences steady population growth and rising service demands, it recognizes that modernization is not
solely a technical requirement, it is a business-driven initiative essential to improving operational performance,
financial stewardship, and customer service delivery.

Evolving the IRCDUS’s technology landscape is central to
meeting current and future expectations, enabling data-driven decision-making, and aligning people, processes, and
platforms with the County’s long-term strategic goals.

This Project reflects IRCDUS’s commitment to modernizing
its technology ecosystem and improving customer experience through better service delivery, data transparency,
and enterprise alignment.

The selected Firm will be expected to address the following priorities:
Customer Experience Improvement
One core objective of this engagement is to improve how IRCDUS interacts with and serves customers.

The future
CIS and supporting systems should enable enhanced customer self-service, personalized communications, real-time

Page 3 of 16

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

consumption alerts, and flexible payment options.

The Consultant should define requirements that support a digitalfirst customer experience and enable Customer Service Representatives (CSRs) to deliver faster, more accurate,
and more empathetic responses.

System Integration and Meter-to-Cash Transparency
The Consultant must emphasize the integration of all critical systems across the meter-to-cash lifecycle, including
CIS, Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), Geographic Information System (GIS),

Computerized Maintenance
Management System (CMMS) for work order management, Finance (ERP), and Document Management Systems
(DMS).

The goal is to enable real-time, end-to-end data transparency that supports accurate billing, proactive
customer outreach, and efficient service call resolution.

System interoperability must reduce handoffs, eliminate
data silos, and provide CSRs with comprehensive access to customer account history, meter data, service orders,
and payment status.

Foundation for Enterprise Transformation
This Project may become part of a broader County initiative to establish a modern, enterprise-wide operating model
that aligns people, technology, and processes.

The Consultant may evaluate the County’s current IT (including
utility operations) holistically and identify strategies that support long-term transformation.

This includes aligning
systems and staffing with industry best practices, standardizing business processes, improving cross-departmental
collaboration, and adopting cloud-first technologies that support scalability, sustainability, and organizational
agility.

Strategic Technology Roadmap (UTMP)
The UTMP must serve as a practical, prioritized roadmap to guide the IRCDUS’s technology investments over the
next five (5) years.

It should provide short-, mid-, and long-term recommendations across infrastructure,
applications, staffing, and governance.

Emphasis should be placed on readiness for cloud migration, cybersecurity
posture, data management practices, systems integrations, and the flexibility to adapt to future technologies and
regulatory changes.

Cybersecurity and Regulatory Compliance
Given the sensitivity of utility customer data and financial transactions, the selected Consultant must ensure that
system requirements and future-state architecture meet modern cybersecurity standards and regulatory obligations.

The Plan should address identity and access management, encryption, audit trails, incident response, disaster
recovery, and system recovery practices.

Organizational Readiness and Change Management
The Consultant must assess IRCDUS’s readiness for change across Departments/Divisions, skill sets, and
organizational culture, and recommend a Change Management strategy that ensures user adoption, minimizes
operational disruption, and builds long-term capability.

Training plans, communications strategies, and stakeholder
engagement should be addressed in both the UTMP development and CIS selection phases.

Total Cost of Ownership and Sustainability
A comparative cost analysis must be developed for CIS solutions and broader IT initiatives, factoring in all
components of ownership, licensing, implementation, hosting, support, integrations, staff resources, and long-term
scalability.

The Consultant should provide budget-aligned recommendations to support capital and operating fiscal
planning cycles.

Project Goals and Objectives
The Consultant will work closely with the County’s Information Technology staff, County departments, and
management stakeholders to perform a high-level analysis of IRCDUS current technology landscape.

The CIS will

Page 4 of 16

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

be addressed early in the engagement due to the urgency of upcoming contract decisions and the system’s
importance to utility billing, customer engagement, and financial management.

As part of the CIS effort, the Consultant will:








Assess the County’s current CIS environment.

Document current business processes, identify potential gaps, and assist with identifying potential process
improvements
Document functional and technical requirements necessary for a user-friendly CIS platform.
Conduct a market scan of available SaaS and on-premises CIS products.
Facilitate vendor engagement, procurement strategy, and contract negotiations.

Deliver a comparative evaluation of viable CIS solutions, including functionality, scalability, vendor
reputation, implementation risk, and five-year total cost of ownership.

Analyze staff resource impacts and risks associated with data conversion, business continuity, and customer
billing during the transition.

Findings related to the CIS will be documented and shared with IRCDUS leadership early in the engagement to
support budget planning and procurement timelines.

In parallel with the CIS selection work, the Consultant will conduct a broader IT assessment across IRCDUS to
develop the UTMP.

This includes evaluating staffing, software and hardware assets, enterprise system usage,
cybersecurity posture, and technology governance.

The analysis will identify gaps and opportunities to improve
business processes, reduce redundancies, and enhance service delivery, particularly through cloud-based
technologies and system integration.

The UTMP must address the following key requirements:
Business-Driven Technology Alignment
The UTMP must be rooted in business priorities, including operational efficiency, customer experience
improvement, regulatory compliance, and financial sustainability.

The Plan must evaluate how technology can
enable core utility and enterprise functions and identify opportunities to streamline and digitize business processes
across departments.

IT Administration and Data Management Responsibility
The Consultant must clearly define what elements of IT administration and data management remain within the
County’s responsibility, particularly as more systems transition to cloud-based platforms.

This includes:



Roles and responsibilities for managing data quality, access, and performance.

Clarifying which parts of system infrastructure and application support can or should be shifted to vendors
under cloud contracts.

Contractual and Cloud Governance Considerations
The UTMP must include guidance for the County on managing cloud-based system contracts, particularly in areas
where vendors embed terms related to bandwidth, storage, or data residency.

The Consultant should:




Identify common pitfalls in cloud service contracts (e.g., hidden bandwidth fees, vague performance terms).
Provide best practices for structuring vendor agreements that protect the County’s interests.

Address concerns around data being hosted in foreign jurisdictions (e.g., Canada) and the potential for
board-level restrictions on data location and access.
Page 5 of 16

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

Integration of Critical Systems for Operational Visibility
The County requires a roadmap for integrating systems for data transparency and decision making.

The UTMP
must:



Identify how systems such as CIS, SCADA, GIS, CMMS, and other operational platforms can be integrated
to provide a transparent, end-to-end view of customer and infrastructure data.

Emphasize the need for Customer Service Representatives to access data such as service history, meterreads, or billing issues from one platform or dashboard to effectively serve customers in real time.

Practical Use of Cloud-Based SCADA and Operational Tools
As cloud-based SCADA systems become more common, the Consultant must evaluate where and how the County
can responsibly adopt cloud for real-time operational systems.

The UTMP must:



Assess the feasibility and timing of moving SCADA and related infrastructure to the cloud.

Provide recommendations on the level of control, latency, and security needed to safely manage utility
infrastructure using remote, vendor-managed platforms.

Data Usability and Reporting Flexibility
The UTMP must address how data can be structured and made usable across departments.

This includes:



Reducing reliance on manual reporting or IT intervention to extract key performance data.

Providing guidance on how to architect systems so staff can independently generate actionable reports, such
as isolating specific data points, without needing custom development or external support.

Change Readiness and System Familiarization
The Consultant must help the County understand what it means to adopt new technologies and platforms at scale.

This includes:



Documenting what adjustments staff must make as systems shift from traditional on-premise to vendormanaged cloud environments.

Identifying steps the County can take now to prepare teams for changes in system access, support models,
and reporting workflows.

Resource Requirements
The Consultant shall provide estimates of the resource requirements with high-level range of costs necessary to
implement the prioritized recommendations defined within the Plan.

These estimates must include both external
implementation costs and internal IRCDUS and/or County resource requirements, identifying the specific roles,
skillsets, and approximate time commitments (full-time equivalent or FTE) needed from staff throughout the
implementation lifecycle.

The cost schedule should be structured to reflect phased investments over time and
aligned with the County’s capacity for adoption and Change Management.

For the CIS in particular, the Consultant will provide a comprehensive resource recommendation strategy to support
successful implementation.
This strategy must outline the critical project roles, governance model, and decisionmaking structure required during the CIS implementation.

The Consultant will also define the internal County
resource needs, specifying both full-time and part-time roles (e.g., project managers, subject matter experts, testing
coordinators, trainers, and operational leads), including time commitment estimates for each phase of the project
(e.g., procurement, design,
testing, deployment, and stabilization).

In addition, the Consultant must provide guidance on the staffing strategy required to maintain business continuity
during the CIS implementation.

This includes identifying operational functions that may be impacted by staff

Page 6 of 16

RFP 2026003 For UTMP CIS Consulting Services

reassignment to the project and recommending appropriate backfill staffing to support day-to-day operations during
the transition.

The County expects the Consultant to leverage their experience to propose effective strategies for
balancing project and operational needs without compromising service delivery.

Deliverables
This UTMP should provide IRCDUS with a practical and informed strategy for transitioning from legacy systems
to modern platforms.

It must focus not only on system upgrades, but also on the necessary operational, contractual,
and organizational shifts required to manage data and deliver utility services effectively in a cloud-first future.

All findings, recommendations, and strategic priorities, including CIS, will be consolidated into the final Utilities
Technology Master Plan.

The UTMP will provide a practical, actionable roadmap that aligns with Indian River
County’s operational objectives, financial plans, and long-term vision for a scalable, resilient, and customer-centric
technology environment.

Method of Selection
The County shall convene a Selection Committee to evaluate all submittals deemed responsive by the Purchasing
Division.
If no submittals are deemed responsive, the selection process will stop, and no contract will be awarded.
The Selection Committee will determine “next steps” should less than two responsive submittals be received.

The responsibility of the Selection Committee shall be as follows:
a.

Each Committee member shall independently review and evaluate each submittal by assigning a number
of points for each criterion, as established in the solicitation, and then totaling the number of points for all
criteria for each Firm.
b.

As a "Committee of the whole", develop a combined ranking order of all Submittals meeting minimum
qualifications.

The ranking of Firms shall be done in the following manner:
1.

The total number of points received by each Firm from all Committee members shall be totaled
and divided by the number of Committee members, to produce an average score.

The Firm receiving the highest average score shall be ranked the # 1 Firm, and the process repeated
until all Firms have been ranked according to their average score.

In the event of a tie, the ranking of tied Firms shall be determined by consensus scoring, based on
discussion on the tied Firms among the committee.

After the initial ranking is established, the Committee may discuss the scores and their reasons
behind them, and each member may modify their ranking or scores of Firms accordingly until the
Committee is satisfied with the rankings.

After interviews, and based upon information learned during the interviews, each Committee
member will rank the Firms in order of preference and a consolidated final Committee ranking
established.
c.

The County may, solely at its own option, seek additional Submittals with this or a similar Submittal in the
event the County, solely at its own option, determines that the quantity and/or quality of Submittals received

County Board of County Commissioners, which shall, at its sole option, authorize negotiations of a contract
pursuant to the requirements of Florida law.
e.

The Indian River County Board of County Commissioners possesses sole authority to award a contract for

General Terms and Conditions
By submitting a Proposal in response to this request, the Firm/Consultant acknowledges the instructions
and information provided herein.
Cone of Silence.

Board of Commissioners, County Administrator, or any County staff other than Purchasing personnel in

Prohibition Against Considering Social, Political or Ideological Interests in Government
Contracting: As provided in section 287.05701, Florida Statutes, as amended, the County may not
request documentation of, or consider a Consultant's social, political,

or ideological interests when
determining if the Consultant is responsible and may not give preference to a Consultant based on its

Right to Protest: Any actual or prospective responding party who is aggrieved in connection with a
competitive selection process may protest to the Purchasing Manager.
